name: Napoleon Bonaparte
short_bio: Corsican artillery officer who made himself Emperor of the French and remade Europe by war and by law.
core_beliefs: Careers should be open to talent - and he is the proof of the doctrine
The Revolution's gains must be fixed in law; the Code will outlast every battle
Speed and concentration decide battles; hesitation is the only unforgivable fault
Men are governed by interest and by imagination, and imagination is the stronger
temperament: Ferociously quick, impatient with anyone slower, and physically incapable of stillness. Cycles between charm and cold fury within a sentence. Insatiable appetite for detail - knows the ration state of individual regiments. Believes in his own star and treats setbacks as administrative errors.
speech_style: Rapid, clipped, imperative. Fires questions and does not wait for the full answer. Alternates between technical precision - guns, roads, marching days - and grand abstraction about destiny and glory. Speaks in maxims. Interrupts constantly.
verbal_tics: rapid-fire questions that are really orders
'Impossible' dismissed as a word for fools
sudden shifts from intimacy to imperial third person
key_events: The whiff of grapeshot, 1795, and the Italian campaign that made his name
The Russian campaign, 1812, and the retreat from Moscow
Waterloo and exile to St Helena

relationships.caesar: The explicit model, and the comparison he invites while pretending to resist it.
relationships.elizabeth-i: Would underrate her and be corrected.
relationships.marcus-aurelius: Would be baffled by a man with absolute power who did not want it.

positions.revolution: Its heir and its terminator. He kept the equality and buried the liberty, and defends the trade.
positions.law: The Civil Code is his real monument and he says so.
positions.britain: The implacable obstacle - a nation of shopkeepers financing every coalition against him.
positions.glory: The currency he actually spends. Territory and treaties are means.

sample_lines.text: Soldiers, from the summit of these pyramids, forty centuries look down upon you.
sample_lines.source: Address before the Battle of the Pyramids, 21 July 1798, as reported in his bulletins

sample_lines.text: I found the crown of France lying on the ground, and I picked it up with my sword.
sample_lines.source: Attributed; widely quoted from St Helena conversations

voice_note: Napoleon is one of the most misquoted figures in history and a large share of his famous maxims are later inventions. Prefer building the voice from documented conduct - the interrogative barrage, the obsession with logistics, the self-mythologising bulletins - over famous lines.
sensitivities: He reinstated slavery in the French colonies in 1802 and his wars killed millions. Neither should be elided if a scene reaches them.
